excerpt: A complete guide to the hours and days after a South Carolina crash: the scene, the report, the insurer, and the deadlines that follow.
keyTakeaways: After a SC accident: call 911, document scene, do not admit fault. SC requires stopping (S.C. Code §§ 56-5-1210, 56-5-1220) and reporting injury crashes to police (§ 56-5-1260). 3-year SOL (S.C. Code § 15-3-530). Mandatory UM coverage (S.C. Code § 38-77-150). Comparative fault bars at 51%. Min insurance 25/50/25. Punitive capped at 3x compensatory or an indexed floor ($739,245 in 2026), with no cap for a driver substantially impaired by alcohol or drugs (S.C. Code § 15-32-530).

faqs.question: What should I do immediately after a SC accident?
faqs.answer: Call 911, check injuries, exchange info, document scene, collect witnesses, do not admit fault. S.C. Code § 56-5-1210 requires stopping.

faqs.question: How long to file in South Carolina?
faqs.answer: 3 years from date of accident (S.C. Code § 15-3-530), but only 2 years if a government vehicle or agency is a defendant (S.C. Code § 15-78-110).

faqs.question: Does SC require UM coverage?
faqs.answer: Yes. S.C. Code § 38-77-150 requires UM coverage on every policy at no less than 25/50/25, and it cannot be waived. Higher UM limits and UIM coverage must be offered but are optional (S.C. Code § 38-77-160).

faqs.question: What is SC comparative fault rule?
faqs.answer: Modified comparative fault with 51% bar: you recover if you were 50% or less at fault, reduced by your percentage; at 51% or more you recover nothing.

faqs.question: What damages can I recover?
faqs.answer: Medical expenses, lost wages, pain and suffering, emotional distress, property damage, loss of enjoyment. Punitive damages are capped at 3x compensatory or an inflation-indexed floor ($739,245 in 2026), with no cap for a driver substantially impaired by alcohol or drugs (S.C. Code § 15-32-530).
